case.case_title: Priyantha Dias v. Ekanayake, Reserve Police Constable, Police Station, Polpithigama and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, SC (Application) No. 860/99, decided on 23 January 2001

clause.text: No person shall be arrested except according to law and must be informed of the reason.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was lawfully arrested in accordance with Article 13(1) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was unlawfully arrested without any basis or reasonable suspicion, violating Article 13(1).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued the petitioner was taken into custody on suspicion due to robberies in the area and failure to provide details about himself.
key_facts: Petitioner was a school teacher waiting at a bus stop with the school principal.
Police officers questioned the petitioner about his place of birth and identity.
Petitioner was accused of being a 'tiger' based on his place of birth (Batticaloa).
Petitioner was forcibly taken on a motorcycle and assaulted by the police officers.
No evidence or reasonable suspicion was presented to justify the arrest.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that Article 13(1) requires any arrest to be lawful and based on reasonable suspicion or procedure established by law, and the arrested person must be informed of the reason.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found no evidence of any reasonable suspicion or complaint against the petitioner and accepted the petitioner’s version that he was arrested without any legal basis, thus violating Article 13(1).
principles_established: Arrest must be based on reasonable suspicion or legal procedure.
Police must have a valid reason and evidence to justify arrest.
Unlawful arrest violates fundamental rights under Article 13(1).

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner’s arrest was unlawful and violated Article 13(1) of the Constitution.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The court ordered compensation to the petitioner and directed payment by the respondents and the State.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(1) was central to the court’s determination that the petitioner’s arrest was unlawful due to lack of reasonable suspicion or legal procedure, directly leading to the finding of violation and remedy.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court found no evidence of reasonable suspicion or complaint against the petitioner and accepted that he was arrested without any basis, violating Article 13(1).
